confirmed.summary: MapDresser connects its late-template handler (AssetLibrary.Ready) and its late-slot handler (InstanceAdded) only after the first dress pass ends. A template that finishes loading after waitAll(25) times out, but before line 308 runs, is never applied to slots that pass already visited.
confirmed.evidence: MapDresser.luau:286 `AssetLibrary.waitAll(MapDresser.WAIT_TIMEOUT)` (25 s), then :290 `dressAll(map)` and :292 `dressAll(Workspace)`. Both yield through `task.wait()` every 40 dressed clones (:258-260). Only after that does :297 connect the AssetSlot InstanceAdded handler and :308 connect `AssetLibrary.Ready`. dressSlot skips any slot whose template `src.get` cannot find yet (:153). AssetLibrary queues all 33 Hero shells, then 53 Props, then 22 Buildings last (AssetLibrary.luau:256-277) at LOAD_CONCURRENCY=4 and LOAD_TIMEOUT=20 (Assets.luau:182-184). That is about 108 loads, so the 25 s wait is often hit while Buildings are still loading. A Ready:Fire during the pass reaches no MapDresser handler, and the Signal does not replay it.
confirmed.failureScenario: Live server, about 1 s per InsertService load: the queue takes about 27 s and MapDresser starts dressing at 25 s. While dressAll is yielding, the `office_block` template finishes after its slots in Map/Buildings were already visited. Its Ready fires before line 308 connects, so every office_block slot keeps its procedural placeholder for the life of that server. Which roles are affected changes from server to server.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Connect the AssetLibrary.Ready handler and the TAG_SLOT InstanceAdded handler at the top of start(), before waitAll and dressAll. Both handlers are already idempotent because dressSlot checks Parent and the Dressed attribute. Alternatively, after the pass, run one more sweep over GetTagged(TAG_SLOT) for every template that is now available.
confirmed.fix: src/server/Systems/MapDresser.luau, start(): move both Connect calls, the TAG_SLOT GetInstanceAddedSignal handler (:297-306) and the AssetLibrary.Ready handler (:308-326), to just after `AssetLibrary.waitAll(MapDresser.WAIT_TIMEOUT)` and before the first dressAll. Both handlers are deferred. dressSlot is non-yielding and idempotent because it checks Parent, Dressed and NoDress, and the pass loop skips slots that a handler has already destroyed. That makes it safe for the handlers to run alongside the pass, and boot still dresses the whole map in one pass after the wait. Connecting at the very top of start() also works, but it dresses slots piecemeal during the 25 s wait.
confirmed.verifyReason: The gap exists but is much narrower than described. MapDresser.start (MapDresser.luau:286-308) calls dressAll(map) and then dressAll(Workspace). The second call collects every AssetSlot under Workspace again, Workspace.Map included, so a template that lands during a yield in the first pass is still picked up for the Map slots the first pass skipped. Luau threads are cooperative and dressSlot never yields. Done:Fire runs its handlers through task.spawn, so control comes back without other threads running. The only time a Ready:Fire can reach no MapDresser handler is therefore during the task.wait() frames inside dressAll(Workspace). Those frames do happen: at 25 s PlotService and DealershipService are still inside their own waitAll(30), so about 50 garage wall-prop slots plus the dealership slots get dressed in that pass, which is more than YIELD_EVERY=40. Map comes first in Workspace's descendant order, so the Map slots have already been visited when that yield happens. A template that finishes during that frame or two, such as a Buildings role, which loads last, keeps its procedural placeholder for the life of the server. PlotService and DealershipService re-dress only their own folders on Ready, so they do not cover this. The window is a frame or two and it only opens when waitAll times out. The fallback is cosmetic, so the severity is low, not medium.

confirmed.summary: Dressing makes every prop non-collidable, including large ones whose procedural placeholders are solid: the plaza fountain, water towers, shipping containers, car crusher, lifeguard towers and the ferris-wheel legs. Whether these objects are solid therefore depends on whether their template loaded on that server.
confirmed.evidence: MapDresser.luau:179-180 sets `d.CanCollide = isBuilding` and `d.CanQuery = isBuilding` for every clone part. It ignores AssetDef.collide and ignores size. MapBuilder `part()` defaults to collide=true (MapBuilder.luau:228), and cyl/ball delegate to part. The placeholders are solid: FountainBasin 28 studs wide (:821), Container (:915), WaterTower Leg/Tank (:849), LifeguardStand/Cabin (:863), CarCrusher Pillar/Beam/Press. ART_PASS.md AP2 budget asks only for 'no colliders on small props (collide=false)'.
confirmed.failureScenario: A player drives across the Spawn Plaza. On a server where the fountain template failed (InsertService outage), the car hits the solid 28-stud basin. On a normal server, the car and the player's character pass straight through the dressed fountain mesh. The same applies to dock shipping containers and the car crusher, which a placeholder made solid cover for chases, and to water-tower legs. The world's collision layout differs between servers and between before and after the dress pass on the same server.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Make props collide when the def says so, or when they are large. For example: `d.CanCollide = isBuilding or def.collide == true or def.size * factor >= LARGE_PROP`. Set collide=true on fountain, shipping_container, car_crusher, water_tower and lifeguard_tower in Config/Assets. Otherwise make the placeholders of those roles non-collidable too, so both states match.
confirmed.fix: Make the collision layout not depend on whether dressing happened. The placeholders are already sized to KIT_DIMS, and MeshPart CollisionFidelity cannot be scripted, so their solid parts make the most reliable collision. In src/server/Systems/MapDresser.luau, in dressSlot, for Category ~= "Buildings": before `slot:Destroy()`, reparent every placeholder BasePart with CanCollide=true into the clone. Set Transparency=1, CastShadow=false and CanTouch=false on each, and remove its decals and SurfaceGuis. Then update tests/spec/mapdress.spec.luau:702 so it checks that dressed props keep the placeholder's colliders. A simpler alternative: use `d.CanCollide = isBuilding or def.collide == true` and the same for CanQuery, and set collide=true on fountain, shipping_container, car_crusher, water_tower, lifeguard_tower, ferris_wheel and crate_stack in src/shared/Config/Assets.luau. That relies on the uploaded meshes' default collision fidelity and still leaves tree trunks inconsistent.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. MapDresser.dressSlot (:179-180) sets CanCollide/CanQuery = isBuilding on every non-root part of a Props clone, which overrides the def.collide value AssetLibrary._normalize applied. tests/spec/mapdress.spec.luau:702 even asserts that props never collide. The MapBuilder placeholders use part(), which defaults to collide=true (MapBuilder.luau:228), and cyl, ball and wedge all go through it. So these placeholders are solid: FountainBasin, Pillar and Bowl (:821-829); WaterTower Leg and Tank (:849-856); LifeguardStand, Cabin, Roof and Ramp (:863-872); Container (:915); CrateStack crates (:922-933); CarCrusher Pillar, Beam, Press and Bed (:960-964); the ferris wheel Hub, Legs and WheelBase (:3256-3277); and the palm and round-tree trunks too. On a normal server, cars and characters pass through the dressed fountain, containers, crusher, ferris-wheel legs, water tower and tree trunks. On a server where a template failed to load, the same objects are solid. ART_PASS.md AP2 asks only for 'no colliders on small props', so making large props ghosts is not what the spec requires. The behaviour is visible and gameplay-relevant in a driving game, but nothing crashes, so medium is right.

confirmed.summary: AssetLibrary loads 12 Props that no slot or system ever uses, and they sit in the queue ahead of every Building. Most are Creator Store assets. They delay AllReady and the colliding building meshes, and they add replicated memory in ReplicatedStorage.
confirmed.evidence: loadQueue (AssetLibrary.luau:267-277) loads every key in Assets.Props before any key in Assets.Buildings. These keys have no consumer anywhere in src (grep): cash_stack, construction_barrier, donut_giant, garage_door_rollup, neon_sign_open, parking_meter, phone_booth, police_barricade, police_helicopter, scrap_car, spray_can, street_lamp_classic. Eleven of them are `source = "store"` (Assets.luau:106-117) and try AssetService first; each can hold one of the 4 load slots for up to LOAD_TIMEOUT=20 s.
confirmed.failureScenario: The store loads are slow or time out, and Buildings start loading only after them. MapDresser's 25 s pass and LoadingScreen's 12 s exit both run with no building meshes, which widens the window in MAPDRESS-LATE-GAP. Every client also downloads the unused police_helicopter and scrap_car templates.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Leave unconsumed keys out of loadQueue: an `unused`/`lazy` flag in AssetDef, or a list of roles actually referenced by slots. Load Buildings before Props, since buildings collide and carry most of the visual weight.
confirmed.fix: In src/shared/Config/Assets.luau, delete the 12 unconsumed Props entries, or add `lazy: boolean?` to AssetDef and have AssetLibrary.loadQueue skip lazy defs in src/server/Systems/AssetLibrary.luau. If you skip them, update tests/spec/assets_shell.spec.luau:114, which expects #queue to equal every entry. Optionally, swap the order to `{ "Buildings", "Props" }` at AssetLibrary.luau:267 so the collidable building meshes load before props.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. A grep of src, excluding Assets.luau, finds no consumer for cash_stack, construction_barrier, donut_giant, garage_door_rollup, neon_sign_open, parking_meter, phone_booth, police_helicopter, scrap_car, spray_can, street_lamp_classic or police_barricade. No slot role and no direct AssetLibrary.get uses them. Eleven are source="store" and police_barricade is owned. flower_bed is used by MapBuilder.flowerBed. AssetLibrary.loadQueue (:267-277) puts all Props, these 12 included, ahead of every Building at LOAD_CONCURRENCY=4. One detail is overstated: a store load usually fails quickly when third-party loading is off, rather than holding a slot for the full 20 s. Even so, they delay Buildings by at least 3 load rounds, and any that do load add replicated templates nobody uses. The cost is boot time and memory, so low.

confirmed.summary: Two Clouds instances end up under Terrain with different settings. MapBuilder now creates one named "Clouds"; LightingService looks only for "HotwireClouds", does not find it, and creates a second.
confirmed.evidence: MapBuilder.luau:3904-3908: `terrain:FindFirstChildOfClass("Clouds") or Instance.new("Clouds")` keeps the default name "Clouds", with Cover 0.45 and Density 0.6. LightingService.luau:513: `getOrCreate(terrain, "Clouds", "HotwireClouds")` checks FindFirstChild("HotwireClouds") only (:337-345), so it adds a second Clouds with Density 0.65. MapBuilder runs before LightingService in ORDER.
confirmed.failureScenario: Every boot leaves Terrain with two Clouds objects. Which one the renderer uses is undefined, and any later tuning in LightingService may have no effect.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Have LightingService reuse `terrain:FindFirstChildOfClass("Clouds")`, or remove the cloud creation from MapBuilder.buildTerrain. Then only one system owns Clouds.
confirmed.fix: Keep a single owner. Either change src/server/Systems/LightingService.luau:513 to `local clouds = (terrain:FindFirstChildOfClass("Clouds") or getOrCreate(terrain, "Clouds", "HotwireClouds")) :: Clouds`, or delete the cloud block at the end of MapBuilder.buildTerrain (src/server/Systems/MapBuilder.luau:3903-3907).
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. MapBuilder.buildTerrain (MapBuilder.luau:3903-3907) is new since 82d7214. It creates or reuses a Clouds named "Clouds" with Cover 0.45 and Density 0.6. LightingService.init (:511-519) runs afterwards in the init phase and calls getOrCreate(terrain, "Clouds", "HotwireClouds"). That function looks up only FindFirstChild("HotwireClouds") (:337-345), so it creates a second Clouds instance. Terrain ends up with two Clouds. The engine is only expected to honour one, and which one is undefined. The settings are nearly identical (Cover is the same, Density 0.6 vs 0.65, both near-white), so the visible impact is negligible. This is mainly a question of which system owns the clouds.

confirmed.summary: Avatar pedestrians keep a HumanoidRootPart that is both collidable and queryable, and no vehicle or police raycast filter excludes Workspace.NPCs. Wheel suspension rays and police line-of-sight rays hit pedestrians, including ones knocked down into the road.
confirmed.evidence: NPCService sanitize (:796-803) clears CanCollide and CanQuery on every part except the root, so the avatar HRP keeps CanQuery=true. spawnStanding then sets `root.CanCollide = true` for walkers (:1532). knockDown launches pedestrians outward at 18-45 studs/s (:1704-1711), so they often land in the lane. VehicleController._refreshFilter (VehicleController.luau:611-622) excludes only the car's own model and player characters, and its params use RespectCanCollide=true (:375-385). PoliceService.refreshLosFilter (:651-663) excludes Vehicles, Effects, Dealership and characters, but not NPCs.
confirmed.failureScenario: A player hits a pedestrian, who tumbles into the road and lies PlatformStanding for 2 s. The next car's wheel rays land on the 2x2x1 root, so the car hops or rides up on it, and a police cruiser behind it gets the same jolt. A pedestrian on the sidewalk between a cruiser and the suspect blocks hasLineOfSight for that tick.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Set `root.CanQuery = false` on NPC roots in spawnStanding; Humanoid floor detection does not need the root to be queryable. Alternatively, add Workspace.NPCs to the VehicleController and PoliceService LOS filter lists.
confirmed.fix: Exclude the NPCs folder in the filters. In src/shared/Vehicle/VehicleController.luau, in _refreshFilter, after inserting self.model, add `local npcs = Workspace:FindFirstChild("NPCs"); if npcs then table.insert(list, npcs) end`. In src/server/Systems/PoliceService.luau, add "NPCs" to the folder list in refreshLosFilter (:652), as ground probing at :883 already does. Do not rely on `root.CanQuery = false`, which has no effect while root.CanCollide is true.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. In NPCService, sanitize (:796-803) excludes the root from the CanCollide/CanQuery clearing, and spawnStanding sets root.CanCollide = true for walkers (:1532). knockDown launches pedestrians at 18-45 studs/s horizontally (:1704-1711), and they lie PlatformStanding for FALL_TIME. The wheel suspension rays in VehicleController (:732) use params with RespectCanCollide=true (:384). _refreshFilter (:607-622) excludes only the car's own model and player characters, so a pedestrian's collidable root is a valid ground hit. PoliceService.refreshLosFilter (:646-663) excludes Vehicles, Effects, Dealership and characters but not NPCs, even though its own ground probe already excludes NPCs (:883). The suggested fix does not work, though. Roblox ignores CanQuery=false on a part with CanCollide=true. With RespectCanCollide=true, the raycast uses CanCollide anyway. The Humanoid also re-enables collision on the torso and head parts. The fix has to go in the filter lists. The effect is cosmetic: a car hops over a fallen pedestrian, or police line of sight is blocked for one tick. Low.

confirmed.summary: On touch devices the radio pill is often mirrored to the left of the speedometer, which puts it inside the PlayerModule thumbstick zone. Its ◀/▶ buttons then eat touches meant for steering.
confirmed.evidence: radioLayout (VehicleClient.luau:244-251) only places the pill on the right when canvasWidth/2 + 176 + 216*scale <= canvasWidth - 262 on touch. Otherwise it returns (1, -(SPEEDO_HALF_WIDTH + RADIO_GAP)), which puts the pill left of the speedometer. Kit.uiScale (Kit.luau:96-107) is min(X/1280, Y/720), so every 4:3 or 16:10 tablet gets a design canvas exactly 1280 wide. With boost 1: 640+176+216 = 1032 > 1018, so the pill is always mirrored, at design x 248..464 (19%..36% of the width) and 12..72 px from the bottom. Phones at the 0.55 scale floor (boost 0.72/0.55 ≈ 1.31) mirror whenever the viewport is under ~793 px wide (iPhone SE/8/8+/13 mini, many Androids). There the pill spans about 12%..35% of the width. VehicleClient.luau:5 says touch steering is the PlayerModule thumbstick. The DynamicThumbstick frame covers the left 40% and the bottom 2/3 of the screen. The Prev/Next buttons are Active TextButtons (Kit.button, lines 555-567), so a touch that starts on them never reaches the thumbstick.
confirmed.failureScenario: An iPad player steering with the left thumb lands on ◀/▶. The station changes (with a Click sound) and the car does not steer. Mid-chase this causes crashes or busts.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Never mirror into the left 40% on touch. When the right side does not fit, stack the pill above the speedometer (or above the HORN/EXIT column) at the same x as the speedometer. Alternatively, on touch, drop the ◀/▶ buttons from a left-side pill and use a single tap-to-cycle area placed on the right cluster. Add a radioLayout unit test for a 1280-wide touch canvas and for a 1212-wide canvas at boost 1.31.
confirmed.fix: In src/client/Controllers/VehicleClient.luau, on touch never put Active radio buttons in x < 0.4*canvasWidth. (1) Let radioLayout also return a width or scale: if the full pill does not fit right of the speedometer, shrink it to the right slot (canvasWidth - 262 - (canvasWidth/2 + 176)). This is 202 px on 1280 tablets, so a pill of about 200 px fits. (2) If even that is too small (small phones), set radioPrev/radioNext.Visible = false so the pill is non-Active and touches fall through to the thumbstick. Then either show the pill as display only, or make cycling a single tap target in the right cluster (for example, turn the pill into a tap-to-cycle TextButton only when it sits on the right, or add a small 📻 roundButton next to HORN/EXIT that does not overlap SPIKES). Update tests/spec/ap4.spec.luau: the 'tablet -> left' assertion must change. Add cases for 1280/touch/boost 1 and 1213/touch/boost 1.31 asserting that no Active button lies in x < 0.4*W.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. DrivingUI uses Kit.screen without touchMin, so on every 4:3 or 16:10 tablet the canvas is 1280 wide and the boost is 1. radioLayout then compares 640+176+216=1032 against 1280-262=1018 and mirrors the pill to design x 248..464, y H-72..H-12. The ap4.spec test even encodes this ('tablet: right side would touch DRIFT -> left'). Phones at the 0.55 floor with a viewport under ~793 px (SE, 8, 8+ at canvas 1280 / boost 1.25) mirror as well. The project itself treats the DynamicThumbstick zone as the left 40%, from 1/3 of the height down (see the verified UI-PHONE-MENU-GRID-THUMBSTICK finding and the C1 fix, which hides the touch menu while driving), and the doc comment says touch steering is that thumbstick. In the mirrored spot both Prev (x 253..301) and Next (x 411..459) are Active TextButtons from Kit.button inside that zone. A touch that begins on them is GUI-processed, so it never starts the stick and it changes the station instead. The panel Frame and the labels are not Active, so only the two buttons steal input. One small correction: the 13 mini (812 px viewport) is currently placed on the right under the viewport math. On that phone the real problem is radio-layout-viewport-vs-safe-canvas.

confirmed.summary: layoutRadio measures the canvas from Camera.ViewportSize, but DrivingUI is laid out in the inset-reduced (CoreUISafeInsets) ScreenGui. On notched phones the pill gets placed on the right and covers the left part of the DRIFT button.
confirmed.evidence: VehicleClient.luau:636 calls VehicleClient.radioLayout(cam.ViewportSize.X / scale, ...). Kit.screen (Kit.luau:113-121) creates DrivingUI with IgnoreGuiInset = false and the default ScreenInsets (CoreUISafeInsets), so in landscape the ScreenGui is narrower than the viewport by the left and right notch insets. The touch buttons sit relative to that narrower canvas: per the comment at line 517, DRIFT spans x W-256..W-156 and y H-128..H-28. HUDController measures its layout from gui.AbsoluteSize (HUDController.luau:1092), but the radio does not. Example, an 844x390 iPhone 12-15 with ~47 px insets on each side at scale 0.55 and boost 1.31: the computed canvas is 1534, so the pill fits on the right (1226 <= 1272). The real canvas is about 1364, so the pill spans x 858..1141 and its ▶ button about 1071..1134. DRIFT starts at 1108, so the two overlap by roughly 27-33 design px for y H-90..H-28. The radio Frame is a later sibling of touchFrame under the same root (lines 520 vs 547, ZIndexBehavior Sibling), so it draws on top and receives the touch.
confirmed.failureScenario: On a notched iPhone, a thumb on the left edge of DRIFT (the hold-to-drift handbrake) hits 'Next station' instead. The drift does not start and the music jumps.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Compute the canvas from ui.gui.AbsoluteSize.X / ui.gui UIScale.Scale, or from root.AbsoluteSize, instead of the camera viewport. Re-run layoutRadio on gui AbsoluteSize changes, not only on ViewportSize changes.
confirmed.fix: In src/client/Controllers/VehicleClient.luau layoutRadio: use local w = ui.gui.AbsoluteSize.X; canvas = (if w >= 1 then w else cam.ViewportSize.X) / scale (this is the same approach as HUDController.canvasSize). Call layoutRadio() after ui.gui.Enabled = true in the enter path (or call it again there). Also connect ui.gui:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize") to layoutRadio (when a session exists) in start(), alongside or instead of the ViewportSize hook. Land this together with the touch-side fix for radio-thumbstick-overlap.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. Kit.screen sets IgnoreGuiInset=false, which (per the ScreenGui docs) means ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets, and that includes the device safe-area insets (notch / cutout) on both sides in landscape. The default SafeAreaCompatibility=FullscreenExtension only extends the background of a fullscreen object such as Root; the enum docs say it 'does not affect the size or position of the descendant's content'. So the touch buttons (anchored to Root's right edge) are laid out in the inset canvas. layoutRadio, however, uses cam.ViewportSize.X / scale. Example, 844x390 with 47+47 insets at scale 0.55 and boost 1.31: the computed canvas is 1534.5, so the pill goes right (1225.6 <= 1272.5). The real canvas is about 1363.6, so the pill spans x 857.8..1140.6 and Next about 1071..1134, against DRIFT x 1107.6..1207.6. That is about 27 px of overlap over y H-83..H-28, and it is worse on 59-px-inset Pro models (about 41 px). Radio is a later sibling of touchFrame under Root, so it draws on top. HUDController already measures gui.AbsoluteSize (line 1092), so this is inconsistent within the codebase. Note: once fixed, these phones will take the mirrored branch, so this must ship together with the radio-thumbstick-overlap fix.

confirmed.summary: New sidewalk pedestrians keep a collidable, queryable HumanoidRootPart, are server-owned and sit in no collision group. Client-owned player cars therefore treat them as immovable boxes, and the shared VehicleController raycast filter does not exclude them.
confirmed.evidence: NPCService.luau:1531-1533 sets root.CanCollide = true ('walkers: the root is their collision box') for unanchored pedestrians. The template sanitizer (lines 796-803) leaves the root's CanQuery true. The roots are SetNetworkOwner(nil) (lines 1712 and 1967), and nothing in src uses CollisionGroup or PhysicsService. VehicleController._refreshFilter (VehicleController.luau:607-622) excludes only the driven model and players' characters, with RespectCanCollide = true (line 384). In Roblox physics an assembly owned by another peer acts as a kinematic obstacle in the owner's simulation. The car is client-owned, so on the driver's client a pedestrian is an unpushable 2x2x1 box. The comic knock-down is meant to come from the server-side _carHitsPed sweep (PED_TICK 0.25 s, line 77). A fallen pedestrian (PlatformStand for FALL_TIME 2 s) still has a collidable root lying on the sidewalk, which the client's suspension rays can hit.
confirmed.failureScenario: A player cuts across a sidewalk at 80+ studs/s during a chase and clips a pedestrian. The car stops dead or bounces and spins as if it hit a post (and may trigger VehicleClient crash shake). On the server the pedestrian is shoved hard. Driving over a fallen pedestrian makes the car hop.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Put NPC parts (pedestrians, ejected ragdolls, officers) in a 'NPC' collision group that does not collide with the vehicle chassis and bump-stop group. Keep the server _carHitsPed sweep as the only knock-down. Also add Workspace.NPCs to VehicleController._refreshFilter and the WheelAnimator bob filter, or set the pedestrian root CanQuery = false.
confirmed.fix: Register collision groups on the server: in NPCService.start, PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup("NPC") and ("Car"), then PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable("NPC", "Car", false). In NPCService sanitize(), set CollisionGroup = "NPC" on every BasePart of the template, so clones, ejected ragdolls and the officer inherit it. In src/shared/Vehicle/CarBuilder.luau, set CollisionGroup = "Car" on the Chassis (setupChassis) and on the BumpStops, guarded with pcall so the Lune harness and client-built display cars still work if the group is not registered. In src/shared/Vehicle/VehicleController.luau newRaycastParams, set params.CollisionGroup = "Car" so suspension rays ignore NPC parts. As an alternative or addition, add Workspace.NPCs to _refreshFilter (and to WheelAnimator's bob filter). Keep _carHitsPed as the only knock-down.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed. In spawnStanding, unanchored walkers get root.CanCollide = true (NPCService.luau:1531-1533). sanitize() clears CanCollide and CanQuery only for non-root parts, so the root stays collidable and queryable. Roots are SetNetworkOwner(nil), and there is no CollisionGroup or PhysicsService usage anywhere in src. The player's car is client-owned, so on the driver's client the server-owned pedestrian root is a replicated, kinematic obstacle. The chassis (CarBuilder setupChassis: bottom about 0.9, height 1.8-1.9, the only collidable body part) overlaps a sidewalk pedestrian's root once the car mounts the 0.6 curb: chassis top about 3.3 vs root bottom about 0.6 + HipHeight (2.0-2.3). Taller vehicles (bottom 2.7) overlap fully, and a fallen pedestrian's root lies right at chassis height. VehicleController._refreshFilter excludes only the car and player characters, and RespectCanCollide=true, so suspension rays also hit a fallen pedestrian's root. The server-side _carHitsPed knock-down runs at 4 Hz on lagged positions, so the client-side collision happens first.

confirmed.summary: The radio labels get only 104 design px between the two 48 px buttons, so station and track names shrink to about 7-9 real px on phones. That is below the project's own ~14 px touch readability floor, and long titles overflow onto the ▶ button.
confirmed.evidence: labelInset = 5 + 48 + 3 = 56 (line 568), so each label is 216 - 112 = 104 design px wide. The station label is TextScaled with Max 18 / Min 9; the title is TextScaled with Max 13 / Min 8 and TextWrapped = false. On a phone at UIScale 0.55 and boost 1.31 (×0.72 overall), 'BASS DROP 101' fits at about 13 design px, which is about 9 real px. A title like '♪ Urban Jungle Drive' needs under 8 design px, gets clamped to Min 8 (about 5.8 real px) and overflows the label. The label is not clipped, so the text runs under or over the Next button. Theme.TouchMinScale (0.72) exists specifically to keep text at least ~14 real px on phones.
confirmed.failureScenario: On a phone the pill shows tiny, illegible text, with titles spilling over the ▶ glyph.
confirmed.suggestedFix: On touch, drop the title line, or make the pill wider and the buttons narrower. Add TextTruncate = AtEnd with no MinTextSize below about 12 design px, and set ClipsDescendants on the label area.
confirmed.fix: In VehicleClient.luau buildUI and layoutRadio, on touch: hide radioTitle and let radioStation use the full pill height, drop the '📻 ' prefix, and narrow or remove the ◀/▶ buttons. This pairs with the tap-to-cycle pill from the thumbstick fix, which frees about 200 px for the label. Use TextScaled = false with a fixed TextSize of at least about 18 design and TextTruncate = AtEnd, so long names truncate instead of shrinking or overflowing. Keep the desktop layout as is.
confirmed.verifyReason: Mostly confirmed. labelInset = 5+48+3 = 56, so both labels are 104 design px wide before the radio UIScale (the boost). On a phone at UIScale 0.55 with boost 1.31 (×0.72 overall), '📻 BASS DROP 101' in FredokaOne (about 8.8 em) fits at about 11.8 design px, which is about 8.5 real px. '♪ Urban Jungle Drive' in GothamBold (about 10 em) fits at about 10.3, which is about 7.4 real px. Both are far below the ~14 real px goal behind Theme.TouchMinScale. However, decide() (:69-77) returns send=true for any boost change regardless of time, so at RATE=6 (:21; Net bucket starts at 6 and caps at 12 tokens, Net.luau:96-118) a client can toggle 6 times a second. Each 'on' edge makes every client within RANGE=300 run flame:Emit(20), toggle a PointLight and play a whoosh (EffectsController.luau:1906-1922). HONK_COOLDOWN=0.3 (:22) relays up to 3.3 horns a second (:1949). Boost is client-trusted: send true once and the 1.5 s keep-alive (:163-164) re-broadcasts flames for as long as the player drives, with no nitro-tank check. Net.fireNear (Net.luau:175-184) also fires to the sender, whose client discards it.

Exclude the sender in broadcast (add a fireNearExcept). Add tests on decide() for edge spam and duration cap.

Every client also composites classic Shirt/Pants per humanoid; spawnDriver and spawnPedestrian give random skin tones (:1368-1370, :1948), which reduces how much composites can be shared.
